CropPilot transparent ranking method; screening scores are not yield predictions

assumptions: FAO-56 crop-stage lengths and coefficients are general reference values; cultivar, region, soil and management change actual crop water use.

Romania is divided into provisional warm, temperate, and cool thermal bands using NASA POWER mean daily temperature for April–September (18°C and 16°C cutoffs); these are project bands, not official agroclimatic regions.
Crop sowing and heat-sensitive months shift by thermal band as project estimates; regional calendars and suitability need Romanian agronomist validation.
Rainfall is compared directly with crop evapotranspiration; runoff, effective rainfall, soil-water storage and drainage are not modeled.
A 10th-percentile historical water-adequacy score is used as the climate-reliability criterion.
The 10th percentile is calculated across valid crop-season observations; it reuses water adequacy and is not an independent climate-risk model.
A crop season is excluded unless at least 90% of its daily observations have both usable ET0 and precipitation.
The soil score is not derived from SoilGrids or user soil measurements because locally validated crop-response thresholds are not yet available.
Adjacent crops from the same botanical family are excluded; if recent crop history is provided, the first crop cannot share its latest known family.
Heat thresholds are literature-based screening levels, not precise local crop-damage limits; cultivar, exposure duration, and night temperatures matter.
Sensitive months are provisional thermal-band calendar estimates, not measured phenology; heat exposure does not affect the current ranking.
Heat-day counts compare daily maximum air temperature with the crop screening threshold in its sensitive month(s); they do not model canopy temperature, exposure duration, or frost.
The soil score is a rotation-structure proxy based on family diversity and a legume phase; it is not a measured soil-carbon or nitrogen change.
